root.name: Benko Gambit Accepted
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6

overview: Black has given a pawn and now offers a second on a6 for open a- and b-files. The main line is 5.bxa6 Bxa6 6.Nc3 d6 7.e4 Bxf1 8.Kxf1 g6 9.g3 Bg7 10.Kg2 O-O 11.Nf3, where White has an extra pawn and a slight centre but a displaced king, and Black has rooks on the open files, a fianchetto bishop on g7 and long-term pressure. White can also decline with 5.Nc3.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn, consolidate with Nc3, e4 and g3, and exploit the central majority.
Return the pawn at the right moment to neutralise Black's pressure.

black_ideas.idea: Pressure the queenside on the a- and b-files with rooks and the g7 bishop.
Play ...Nbd7, ...Qa5 and ...Rb8; trade the light bishops.

typical_structures.structure: White pawn majority on the kingside and centre against Black's pressure on the open a- and b-files.

character.notes: Long-term compensation rather than short tactics; White is a pawn up but Black has a stable game with few ways to lose quickly.

gambit.notes: Black has sacrificed a pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: A respected gambit; fully sound with correct play.

structure.notes: Half-open a- and b-files for Black against a White centre.

approach.notes: A recognised choice at every level, though it is a specific gambit rather than a system.

level.notes: Plans are clear (rooks on files), moderate theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.Nc3
sublines_that_differ.how: White declines to take on a6 and offers a different structure.

character.reason: A long-term strategic plan, neither forcing nor especially hard to crack.

gambit.reason: Black sacrifices a pawn White can keep.

structure.reason: Half-open a- and b-files for Black.

level.reason: Clear plans with moderate theory; the compensation takes feel.

plans.reason: Pressure on the queenside with a long diagonal bishop.
